task.text: What is the main difference between IP over Asynchronous Transfer Mode (ATM) and IP over Ethernet (Ethernet)?

attempts.high: I'm putting together teaching material on layer-2 transport for IP and I want a fresh angle. Come up with your own way to explain how IP over ATM differs from IP over Ethernet — invent an analogy, a scenario, whatever framing you think lands best for newcomers. Your call on structure and examples, just make the core distinction click.
attempts.low: Using only these two given facts — (1) ATM is connection-oriented and uses fixed 53-byte cells, (2) Ethernet is connectionless and uses variable-length frames — state in one or two sentences what the main difference is between IP over ATM and IP over Ethernet. Don't add other points, just restate the distinction these facts imply.
